 You followed this author

 Marcos is immune from any impeachment case until January 2027, following the one-year bar rule 
 AT A GLANCE
 The Supreme Court did not rule on or recommend the impeachment of President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., despite claims circulating on social media.
 Marcos is protected from new impeachment proceedings until January 2027 due to the one-year immunity rule following previous complaints that were dismissed.
 The false claim originated from the SC's ruling on the 2024 and 2025 national budgets, which declared certain appropriations unconstitutional but did not mention impeachment.
 This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors . 
 Claim: The Supreme Court (SC) has opened the possibility of impeaching President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. in relation to its ruling declaring the 2024 and 2025 national budgets as unconstitutional.
 Rating: FALSE 
 Why we fact-checked this: Facebook user Gamol Adam Bustalino posted a social media graphic containing the claim, with a photo of Marcos and the SC logo.
 Text on the graphic reads, “Korte Suprema, nagbukas ng posibilidad ng impeachment laban kay PBBM.”  
 (Supreme Court opens possibility of impeachment against [President Bongbong Marcos].)
 The Facebook post has 10,500 reactions, 1,600 comments, and 716 shares as of writing. Several social media users in the comments section also praised the High Court for its supposed move.
 The facts: The SC did not rule on or recommend Marcos’ impeachment. 
 The President enjoys one year of immunity from any new impeachment case until January 2027, following the one-year bar rule. 
 According to Article XI, Section 3(5) of the 1987 Constitution , an impeachable official like the President can only undergo one impeachment proceeding per year. Two impeachment complaints were already filed against Marcos in January that accused him of violating the Constitution, graft and corruption, and betrayal of public trust. These were later dismissed in February due to insufficiency in substance. 
 SC ruling on budget laws: The false claim stemmed from the SC’s October 20 ruling, which declared the 2024 and 2025 General Appropriations Acts unconstitutional because of unauthorized increases in unprogrammed appropriations by Congress.
 In its ruling, the High Tribunal wrote that while the doctrine of operative fact preserves irreversible programs whose beneficiaries acted in good faith, it does not shield the authors, proponents, or implementers of the unconstitutional budget provisions from liability. (READ: 5 practical effects of SC ruling on unprogrammed appropriations )
 On October 21, SC Spokesperson Camille Ting said that proper cases against relevant public officials should be filed in the appropriate tribunals . 
 Contrary to the claim, however, the SC did not explicitly call for or suggest initiating impeachment proceedings against Marcos. Impeachment is a power vested exclusively in Congress. (READ: FAST FACTS: How does impeachment work? )
 Previous fact checks: Rappler has debunked numerous false allegations of Marcos’ supposed ouster or impeachment:

 FACT CHECK: No reports of SC order ousting Marcos  
 FACT CHECK: Toby Tiangco did not say Marcos will be impeached in 2027  
 FACT CHECK: Congress did not vote on any new impeachment case vs Marcos

 – Eirene Manatlao/Rappler.com
